name: Nick Walshe
title: Senior media trainer and broadcast journalist
bio_short: Senior media trainer and broadcast journalist with more than 30 years' experience. Former BBC, ITV News and Al Jazeera English. Clients include Emirates, Qatar Airways, NEOM, Rolls Royce and the UAE Central Bank. Based in Dubai.
bio: Nick is a senior media trainer with more than 30 years' experience as an international broadcast journalist. He trained at the BBC and spent 15 years with ITV News and ITN as a reporter, presenter, producer and senior editor before joining the management team that launched Al Jazeera English in 2006, where he ran the channel's reporting division and oversaw global content and breaking news.  Since founding his own media consultancy in Dubai in 2010, Nick has specialised in training senior executives, government officials and corporate spokespeople in media skills, presentation and crisis communication. He spent several years embedded as an advisor in a senior government communications office, and his clients include Emirates Airline, Qatar Airways, NEOM, the UAE Ministry of Investment, Rolls Royce, IKEA, Standard Chartered, the Saudi Capital Markets Authority and the UAE Central Bank. Long-term projects include a three-year crisis and reputation programme for Expo 2020 Dubai, a three-year media training programme for Qatar Airways and training programmes for exhibitors and managers at COP28.  At ISOC, Nick delivers media training, crisis communication and presentation skills programmes for senior executives and spokespeople across government, aviation, energy and financial services. He is based in Dubai and trains in English. His continued work in active journalism means his training reflects current media practice.

His clients include Emirates Airline, Qatar Airways, NEOM, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the UAE Ministry of Investment, Rolls Royce, IKEA, Standard Chartered, JP Morgan, the Saudi Capital Markets Authority, ADNOC and the UAE Central Bank. Nick also directs and produces corporate video for clients including ADNOC, Mars and the British Council, and continues to train journalists and provide consultancy for media organisations across Saudi Arabia, Oman, Pakistan, India and the wider region. At ISOC, he delivers media training, crisis communication and presentation skills programmes for senior executives and spokespeople across government, aviation, energy and financial services. He is based in Dubai and trains in English. His experience launching Al Jazeera English and his continued involvement in active journalism mean his training reflects the realities of today's media landscape.
